title: My Day in Order
bigQuestion: How can a few small Spanish words turn a list of actions into a day someone can follow?

story.title: A Day with Sofía in San Juan
story.kicker: Sofía lives in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and she tells her whole day in order.
paragraphs: Sofía is ten years old. She lives in San Juan, the capital of Puerto Rico. In Puerto Rico, people speak Spanish and English. Sofía speaks both. Today she tells us her day in Spanish, one step at a time.

"Primero, desayuno." (First, I eat breakfast.) Sofía eats bread and fruit in the kitchen. It is la mañana (the morning). "Luego, voy a la escuela." (Then, I go to school.) She walks with her little brother. The sun is already warm.

At school, Sofía reads and writes. "Leo un libro." (I read a book.) At lunch she says, "Como arroz con habichuelas." (I eat rice and beans.) After lunch she plays outside with her friends. "Juego con mis amigos." (I play with my friends.)

"Después, voy a casa." (After that, I go home.) It is la tarde (the afternoon). She does her homework at the table. Outside, she hears a tiny frog sing: "co-quí, co-quí." The coquí is a small frog famous in Puerto Rico.

It is la noche (the night) now. Sofía looks at the clock. "Son las nueve." (It is nine o'clock.) "Finalmente, duermo." (Finally, I sleep.) Her day had a first step, middle steps and a last step. That order makes her story easy to follow.
story.think: Sofía used primero, luego, después and finalmente. Which of those words would you use to tell the first thing you do each morning?

sections.title: Words That Put Things in Order

lessons.title: Primero and Luego
lessons.mainIdea: Primero means first and luego means then; they start the first and next steps of a day.
reading: Picture your morning. You wake up. You eat. You go to school. In Spanish, you can show the order with small words. The first step starts with *primero* (first). "Primero, desayuno." means "First, I eat breakfast."
The next step starts with *luego* (then, later). "Luego, voy a la escuela." means "Then, I go to school." Put the order word at the start of the sentence. Put a comma after it, just like in English.
A common mistake is to say "primer" alone for "first" in a list of steps. When you mean "first, I do this," say primero. Another mistake is to forget the comma. Say it: Primero, como. Luego, leo.

words.d: first — starts the first step: Primero, desayuno (First, I eat breakfast)
then, later — starts the next step: Luego, voy a la escuela

look.title: Two Steps in the Morning
look.text: Mateo tells his morning. "Primero, desayuno." (First, I eat breakfast.) "Luego, voy a la escuela." (Then, I go to school.) Primero comes before luego. The order words go at the start of each sentence.
look.prompt: Tell two things you do in the morning. Start one with primero and the other with luego.

check.q: What does primero mean?
check.why: Primero means first. It starts the first step in a list.

check.q: Which sentence means "Then, I go to school"?
check.why: Luego means then, and voy means I go. The order word goes first, with a comma.

check.q: Mateo says: "Luego, leo. Primero, como." What does he do first?
check.why: Primero, como means First, I eat. Primero marks the first step, even if he says it second.

lessons.title: Después and Finalmente
lessons.mainIdea: Después means after that and finalmente means finally; finalmente marks the last step.
reading: Your day keeps going after school. To add another step, use *después* (after that, afterward). "Después, voy a casa." means "After that, I go home." Look at the accent mark on the last e: des-PUÉS.

To tell the very last step, use *finalmente* (finally). "Finalmente, duermo." means "Finally, I sleep." It sounds a lot like the English word finally. Words that look alike in two languages help you guess.

A common mistake is to drop the accent in después. Without it, the word is spelled wrong. Another mistake is to use finalmente in the middle. Save it for the end. Try it: Después, leo. Finalmente, duermo.

words.d: after that, afterward — adds a later step: Después, voy a casa
finally — marks the last step: Finalmente, duermo (Finally, I sleep)

look.title: The End of the Day
look.text: Lucía tells her evening. "Después, voy a casa." (After that, I go home.) "Después, como." (After that, I eat.) "Finalmente, duermo." (Finally, I sleep.) You can use después more than once, but finalmente only once, at the end.
look.prompt: Tell the last two things you do at night. Use después and finalmente.

check.q: Which word is spelled correctly?
check.why: The word is después, with the accent on the last e.

check.q: What does "Finalmente, duermo" mean?
check.why: Finalmente means finally, and duermo means I sleep.

check.q: Where does finalmente belong in a list of steps?
check.why: Finalmente marks the last step, so it goes at the end.

lessons.title: Putting Steps in Order
lessons.mainIdea: Use primero, luego, después and finalmente in that order to tell four steps clearly.
reading: Now use all four words together. Think of making a sandwich. First, you get bread. Then, you add cheese. After that, you close it. Finally, you eat it. Spanish uses the same kind of chain.
Here is Sofía's morning: "Primero, desayuno. Luego, voy a la escuela. Después, leo. Finalmente, como." Each word is a signpost. It tells the listener where we are in the day: start, next, later, end.

The usual order is primero, luego, después, finalmente. Luego and después can swap places. Both mean a later step. But primero always starts, and finalmente always ends. A mixed-up order confuses the listener.

words.d: the order — the way steps follow each other: primero, luego, después, finalmente
the step — one action in a list, like Primero, desayuno

look.title: Mixed-Up Steps
look.text: These steps are mixed up: "Finalmente, duermo." "Primero, desayuno." "Después, voy a casa." "Luego, voy a la escuela." Read the order words. Primero comes first. Luego and después come in the middle. Finalmente comes last.
look.prompt: Put the four sentences in the right order and read them aloud.

check.q: Which order word should come last?
check.why: Finalmente means finally, so it marks the last step.

check.q: Which list is in the usual order?
check.why: The usual chain is first, then, after that, finally: primero, luego, después, finalmente.

check.q: Which two words can swap places in the middle?
check.why: Luego and después both mean a later step, so either can come in the middle.

sections.title: Times of Day and Days of the Week

lessons.title: Morning, Afternoon and Night
lessons.mainIdea: La mañana is the morning, la tarde is the afternoon and la noche is the night.
reading: Think of three parts of your day. You eat breakfast in *la mañana* (the morning). You finish school in *la tarde* (the afternoon, and early evening). You go to bed in *la noche* (the night).
All three words are feminine, so they use la. To say "in the morning," Spanish says por la mañana. "Leo por la noche" means "I read at night." English says in or at, but Spanish uses por here.
Watch out: mañana without la means tomorrow. "La mañana" is the morning. "Mañana" alone is tomorrow. Also, la tarde can mean the afternoon and the early evening, until it gets dark.

words.d: the morning — Desayuno por la mañana (I eat breakfast in the morning)
the afternoon and early evening — Voy a casa por la tarde
the night — Duermo por la noche (I sleep at night)

look.title: Three Parts of a Day
look.text: Picture a window. In the first picture, the sun comes up: la mañana. In the second, the sun is high and school is over: la tarde. In the third, the sky is dark with stars: la noche.
look.prompt: Say one thing you do por la mañana, one por la tarde and one por la noche.

check.q: What does la noche mean?
check.why: La noche is the night, when it is dark.

check.q: How do you say "I read in the afternoon"?
check.why: Spanish uses por la tarde for in the afternoon, and tarde is feminine, so it takes la.

check.q: What does mañana mean when it has no la in front?
check.why: Mañana alone means tomorrow. La mañana means the morning.

lessons.title: The Seven Days
lessons.mainIdea: The days are lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado and domingo, written with small letters.
reading: Look at a Spanish calendar. The week usually starts on lunes (Monday), not Sunday. Then come martes (Tuesday), miércoles (Wednesday), jueves (Thursday) and viernes (Friday).

The weekend is *el sábado* (Saturday) and domingo (Sunday). Notice the accents: miércoles and sábado. In Spanish, the days are written with small letters. English uses capital letters, so English speakers often get this wrong.
To say "on Monday," Spanish uses el: "El lunes, voy a la escuela." Do not add en. Saying "en lunes" is a common mistake that comes from English "on." For every Monday, say los lunes.

words.d: Monday, or on Monday — the first day of the week on Spanish calendars
Saturday, or on Saturday — written with an accent on the first a
the week — seven days, lunes to domingo

look.title: The Week in Order
look.cite: Order of days as shown on most Spanish-language calendars
look.prompt: Which day is number 3? Which two days make the weekend?

check.q: Which day comes right after miércoles?
check.why: The order is lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves. Jueves (Thursday) comes after miércoles.

check.q: How do you say "On Friday, I play"?
check.why: Spanish uses el for on with a day and writes the day with a small letter: El viernes.

check.q: Which day is spelled correctly?
check.why: Sábado has an accent on the first a and, in a sentence, a small s.

lessons.title: My Week, Day by Day
lessons.mainIdea: Put a day at the start of a sentence to tell what you do on that day.
reading: Now join days and actions. Think of your own week. "El lunes, voy a la escuela." (On Monday, I go to school.) "El sábado, juego fútbol." (On Saturday, I play soccer.) The day tells when.
Add a part of the day to be even clearer. "El domingo por la mañana, como con mi abuela." means "On Sunday morning, I eat with my grandmother." The day comes first, then the part of the day.
Use los to show a habit. "Los martes, leo en la biblioteca" means "On Tuesdays, I read at the library." El martes is one Tuesday. Los martes is every Tuesday. The day word does not change.

words.d: Sunday, or on Sunday — the last day of the week on Spanish calendars
on Tuesdays, every Tuesday — los shows a habit; the word martes stays the same

look.title: Diego's Week
look.text: Diego tells his week. "El lunes, voy a la escuela." (On Monday, I go to school.) "Los miércoles, juego básquetbol." (On Wednesdays, I play basketball.) "El domingo por la tarde, leo." (On Sunday afternoon, I read.)
look.prompt: Tell what you do on two different days. Start each sentence with el or los and a day.

check.q: What does "Los sábados, juego" mean?
check.why: Los with a day shows a habit: on Saturdays, every Saturday.

check.q: Which sentence means "On Sunday morning, I eat"?
choices: El domingo por la noche, como.
El domingo por la mañana, como.
El lunes por la mañana, como.
check.why: Domingo is Sunday and por la mañana is in the morning.

check.q: Which word shows a habit, like every Monday?
check.why: Los lunes means on Mondays, every Monday. El lunes is just one Monday.

lessons.title: Verbs for My Day
lessons.mainIdea: Como, voy, juego and leo tell what I do; the -o ending means I.
reading: Think of four things you do every day. You eat, you go places, you play and you read. In Spanish: *como* (I eat), *voy* (I go), *juego* (I play) and *leo* (I read). Each one already means "I."

Look at the endings. Com-o, jueg-o, le-o. The -o at the end tells us the speaker is yo (I). That is why you do not need to say yo. "Como" alone is a full sentence: I eat. Voy is special, but it also means I.

A common mistake is to use the dictionary form. "Yo comer" is wrong. The right way is "Yo como" or just "Como." Another mistake: juego has a u inside it. The dictionary form is jugar, but I play is juego.

words.d: I eat — from comer: Como arroz (I eat rice)
I go — from ir: Voy a la escuela (I go to school)
I play — from jugar: Juego con mis amigos
I read — from leer: Leo un libro (I read a book)

look.title: From Dictionary Form to I
look.text: comer (to eat) → como (I eat). leer (to read) → leo (I read). jugar (to play) → juego (I play). ir (to go) → voy (I go). The first two follow the pattern: drop the ending, add -o. Juego and voy change more, so learn them by heart.
look.prompt: Say three sentences about your day using como, voy and leo.

check.q: How do you say "I read a book"?
check.why: Leo means I read. Leer is the dictionary form and cannot stand for I.

check.q: What does "Voy a casa" mean?
check.why: Voy means I go, and a casa means home.

check.q: Which is the right form for "I play"?
check.why: Jugar changes u to ue, so I play is juego.

lessons.title: It Is One O'Clock
lessons.mainIdea: Ask ¿Qué hora es? and answer Es la una for one o'clock.
reading: Your friend asks, "*¿Qué hora es?*" (What time is it?). Look at the clock. If the short hand is on 1, say "Es la una." (It is one o'clock.) Notice es, not son, because one is only one.
Why la? In Spanish, the word hora (hour) is feminine and hidden in the sentence. La una means la una hora, the first hour. So times always use la or las, never el.
A common mistake is "Son la una." One is singular, so use es. Another mistake is "Es uno." The number must be una, the feminine form, to match hora. Say it: ¿Qué hora es? Es la una.

words.d: What time is it? — the question for telling time
the hour, the time — a feminine word, so times use la and las
It is one o'clock — uses es because one is singular

look.title: Lunch at One
look.text: Ana looks at the clock at school. The short hand is on 1 and the long hand is on 12. Her friend asks, "¿Qué hora es?" Ana says, "Es la una." (It is one o'clock.) Then she adds, "Como a la una." (I eat at one.)
look.prompt: Ask a partner ¿Qué hora es? and answer for one o'clock.

check.q: It is 1:00. What do you say?
check.why: One is singular, so use es, and hora is feminine, so use la una.

check.q: What does ¿Qué hora es? mean?
check.why: Hora means hour or time, so ¿Qué hora es? asks the time.

check.q: Why do Spanish times use la or las?
choices: because the hidden word hora is feminine
check.why: Times stand for la hora or las horas, and hora is a feminine word.

lessons.title: Two, Three and More O'Clock
lessons.mainIdea: For two o'clock and later, say Son las and the number: Son las tres.
reading: Now the clock says 3:00. More than one hour has passed, so Spanish uses the plural. "*Son las tres.*" means "It is three o'clock." Son is the plural form of es, and las is the plural of la.
The pattern works for every hour from two to twelve. Son las dos. Son las cinco. Son las doce. To say at a time, use a: "Voy a la escuela a las ocho." (I go to school at eight.)
Add the part of the day to be clear. "Son las tres de la tarde" means 3:00 in the afternoon. "Son las nueve de la noche" means 9:00 at night. Common mistake: "Es las tres." Use son with plural hours.

words.d: It is three o'clock — son and las because more than one hour
at eight o'clock — a means at when you tell when something happens

look.title: Sofía's School Day (example times)
look.cite: Example schedule made up for this lesson
look.prompt: At what time does Sofía go to school? Say it in Spanish: Voy a la escuela a las…

check.q: It is 3:00. What do you say?
check.why: Three is plural, so use son las: Son las tres.

check.q: What does "Como a las doce" mean?
check.why: Como means I eat, and a las doce means at twelve o'clock.

check.q: How do you say 9:00 at night?
choices: Son las nueve de la noche.
Son las nueve de la mañana.
Es la nueve de la noche.
Son las nueve de la tarde.
check.why: Nine is plural, so son las nueve; de la noche means at night.

review.q: Which word starts the first step of a routine?
review.why: Primero means first, so it starts the list.

review.q: What does "Después, voy a casa" mean?
review.why: Después means after that, and voy a casa means I go home.

review.q: In the story, what is the coquí?
choices: a small frog famous in Puerto Rico
review.why: The coquí is a tiny frog known for its song, co-quí, in Puerto Rico.
Spanish uses el with a day, a small letter and an accent: el miércoles.
One is singular, so es la una.

review.q: What does "Leo por la noche" mean?
review.why: Leo means I read, and por la noche means at night.

review.q: Which sentence is correct for "I eat rice"?
review.why: Como already means I eat. The -o ending tells us the speaker is yo.

review.q: Sofía goes to school at 8:00. Which sentence says that?
choices: Voy a la escuela a la ocho.
Voy a la escuela a las ocho.
Voy a la escuela en ocho.
review.why: At eight o'clock is a las ocho, with the plural las.
